description: The content of config.yaml; every field is optional.

additionalProperties.description: Holds the defaults for one agent.

api_key.description: The agent's API key, written here. Set at most one of api_key, api_key_env and api_key_file; config.yaml must then not be readable by other users. A subscription login in the project is kept.

api_key_env.description: The environment variable on this computer that holds the agent's API key.

api_key_file.description: A file on this computer that holds the agent's API key.

effort.description: The reasoning effort `codeflower task` asks for (the agent's thought level, e.g. low, medium or high).

model.description: The model `codeflower task` asks the agent for, as the agent names it; the task stops when the agent has no such model.

options.description: Other settings of the agent for `codeflower task`, by the ids the agent gives them (as with `--option ID=VALUE`).

agents.description: Settings of each agent, by its id.

connect_only.description: Never start sandboxes here, e.g. on a login node.

notifications.description: Tell the desktop when a chat waits for an answer or ends its turn (default true).

tray.description: Show an icon in the system tray or menu bar where there is one (default true).

wrap_up_minutes.description: How long quitting waits at most for the chats in the client's sandboxes to wrap up (default 10).

engine.description: Auto, docker, podman or apptainer, for the sandboxes the command line starts when neither --engine nor $CODEFLOWER_ENGINE is set.

env_dir.description: A folder for what the projects can download or rebuild (software environments, caches, the chats' browsers), e.g. on scratch, when --env-dir is not given; each project gets a subfolder. Unset, they stay in the project.

image.description: The sandbox image (a Docker/Podman image name or an Apptainer .sif file) for the sandboxes the command line starts when neither --image nor $CODEFLOWER_IMAGE is set.

images.description: Configures the image model codeflower-sketch generates icons with.

api_key.description: The provider's API key, written here (at most one of api_key, api_key_env and api_key_file).

api_key_env.description: The environment variable on this computer that holds the key.

api_key_file.description: A file on this computer that holds the key.

provider.description: Openai or google. An isolated sandbox may reach its API.

isolate_network.description: Start the command line's sandboxes as with --isolate-network.

jobs.description: Lets the agents ask the app to submit batch jobs, each run in a sandbox of its own.

account.description: Charged for the jobs (Slurm's --account), when set.

approve.description: Ask (the default) shows each submission in the chat for the user to allow or deny; never submits what is within the limits without asking, as unattended tasks need.

codeflower.description: The app on the nodes jobs run on (default: this app's path, which must be on a folder they share).

defaults.description: What a job gets that does not ask for it.

engine.description: Runs the jobs' sandboxes: docker, podman or apptainer (default: the sandbox's own). Apptainer starts an image file on a shared folder fastest on clusters whose Podman keeps images per job.

engine_args.description: Container engine flags for the jobs' sandboxes, as --engine-args takes them, e.g. '--gpus all'.

env_writable.description: Lets jobs change the project's software environments; by default they mount them read-only, so jobs running at once cannot break them.

extra.description: Scheduler options added to every job, as the profile's script writes them (Slurm: e.g. --export=NONE, --qos=normal).

limits.description: The most a job, and all of a project's jobs, may ask for.

active.description: Jobs of a project queued or running at once (default 20).

notes.description: Told to the agent with the queues and limits: what to know about this cluster when submitting.

on_stop.description: Keep (the default) leaves a project's jobs running when its sandbox stops, and the next sandbox of the project follows them again; cancel cancels them.

poll.description: How often the jobs' states are asked for (default 1m, at least 15s).

queues.description: Queues, when set, are the only queues (Slurm partitions) jobs may use, each with its own limits; they are listed to the agent.

items.description: A queue jobs may use, with its own limits within Limits.

gpu_types.description: The queue offers, if jobs may name one.

gpus.description: A job of the queue may ask for; 0: none.

scheduler.description: Off (the default), auto (the one whose commands are found here), slurm, local (background jobs on this computer), or the name of a profile under schedulers: or in <config dir>/schedulers/NAME.yaml.

additionalProperties.description: Tells the app how to use a batch scheduler: a template of the batch script, and the commands that submit, list, look up and cancel jobs. Each command is a list of arguments, each a template of its own; none goes through a shell.

array_index_env.description: The variable that holds an array task's index in the job.

command.description: The program and its arguments, each a template.

id.description: ID, for submit, is a regular expression whose first group is the job's id in the command's output (default: the whole first line).

line.description: Line, for status and history, is a regular expression matched against each line of the output, with the named groups id and state (and index and exit for history).

stdin.description: Feeds the batch script to the command (LSF's bsub < script).

detect.description: Commands whose presence on PATH means this scheduler, for scheduler: auto.

extends.description: Names a profile whose fields this one starts from, e.g. slurm.

history.description: History, optional, looks up finished jobs (Slurm's sacct).

command.description: The program and its arguments, each a template.

id.description: ID, for submit, is a regular expression whose first group is the job's id in the command's output (default: the whole first line).

line.description: Line, for status and history, is a regular expression matched against each line of the output, with the named groups id and state (and index and exit for history).

stdin.description: Feeds the batch script to the command (LSF's bsub < script).

pass_env.description: The scheduler's variables the job's sandbox gets.

script.description: The batch script, a Go text/template (docs/jobs.md lists its fields and functions).

states.description: Sort the scheduler's states into queued, running, done, failed and cancelled; a trailing * matches any rest, and "*" alone anything.

command.description: The program and its arguments, each a template.

id.description: ID, for submit, is a regular expression whose first group is the job's id in the command's output (default: the whole first line).

line.description: Line, for status and history, is a regular expression matched against each line of the output, with the named groups id and state (and index and exit for history).

stdin.description: Feeds the batch script to the command (LSF's bsub < script).

command.description: The program and its arguments, each a template.

id.description: ID, for submit, is a regular expression whose first group is the job's id in the command's output (default: the whole first line).

line.description: Line, for status and history, is a regular expression matched against each line of the output, with the named groups id and state (and index and exit for history).

stdin.description: Feeds the batch script to the command (LSF's bsub < script).

submit_file.description: SubmitFile, when set, is a second template written next to the script (as .SubmitFile), for schedulers that take a description of the job (HTCondor) rather than a script.

supports.description: What the script can express of array, after, gpus, account and queue; a job that asks for anything else is refused.

schedulers.description: Profiles of other schedulers, by name: how to write their batch scripts and run their commands (docs/jobs.md).

setup.description: Shell lines the batch script runs before the job's sandbox starts, e.g. `module load apptainer`.

additionalProperties.description: A Model Context Protocol server the agent of every sandbox may use: a command that runs in the sandbox (stdio), or a server at a URL.

command.description: The program that runs the server in the sandbox (stdio).

headers.description: HTTP headers sent to a server at a URL, e.g. Authorization.

transport.description: Of a server at a URL: http (streamable HTTP, the default) or sse, which Codex and dsh do not support.

url.description: The address of a server that runs elsewhere, instead of a command.

mcp_servers.description: The MCP servers given to the agent of every sandbox, by name.

items.description: One of an agent's own plugins under plugins: (docs/plugins.md).

enabled.description: Defaults to true; a project can switch an entry off.

source.description: Agent-neutral: marketplace:NAME@CATALOG, github:OWNER/REPO[#REF], git:URL[#REF], npm:PACKAGE@VERSION, url:https://….zip|.tgz[#sha256=…] or path:/absolute; each agent takes the kinds its descriptor names.

plugins.description: The agents' own plugins every sandbox gets, by agent id.

projects_dir.description: The folder of projects started by name, when --projects-dir is not given (default ~/codeflower/projects). ~ and $VARIABLES are expanded in it and EnvDir, and relative paths are in the config directory.

skills.description: More folders of skills, mounted read-only in every sandbox besides <config dir>/skills; relative paths are in the config directory.

tunnel.description: Configures remote access through a code flower tunnel (`codeflower tunnel login`).

eu_only.description: Routes the tunnel only through EU datacenters. Unset until the first `codeflower tunnel login` asks.

hardened.description: Limits each paired browser to the workers chosen when pairing, and runs the connector as a separate, confined process.

manage.description: Lets remote browsers browse folders, start sandboxes and forget them; without it they use and stop existing sandboxes only.

url.description: The tunnel; the hosted one when empty.
